az_auto_shop_the.blurb: A small trad crag in the Granite Dells near Prescott, one of the walls grouped under the Oasis and reached from Granite Gardens Drive. It holds eight climbs, all trad: a pair of very easy lines, a cluster between 5.7 and 5.9, and one stiffer climb in the 5.11 range. The wall is sunny and sits beside a loop trail that climbs away from the creek, a short way past a neighbouring wall. Expect short, moderate outings that suit a quick session with a small rack.

az_teddy_bear_slabs.blurb: A slabby, wavy-faced formation in the Nursery group in the Bear Canyon section of Mount Lemmon, close to the Catalina Highway. Eight routes mix sport, top-rope and a single trad line, running from about 5.5 up to the 5.10 range, with most in the 5.6 to 5.8 band. Several lines involve working over bulges. Bolts were added in 2025 so every route can now be led. Across the Nursery, most formations catch sun for much of the day, with some morning shade. The quick approach and mellow grades make it a friendly spot for newer climbers.

az_green_acres_north_face.blurb: A small, lush north-facing crag on the Green Slabs side of Mount Lemmon, just off the Catalina Highway. Eight routes, split evenly between sport and trad, sit between 5.9 and 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. The wall never gets direct sun, so it stays cool. The rock is fractured, with twisting, undulating features that force unusual moves; it feels unnerving but holds together, so belayers should wear a helmet. The approach is short, ending in a bushwhack up from a wash.
az_green_acres_north_face.parking_note: Leave the car in the pullout at mile marker 9.9 on the summit-bound side of the Catalina Highway, the east side of the road. The same pullout serves the Green Slabs southwest face.

az_7_lorax_ball_return.blurb: Two neighbouring gullies in the Chessman Area of Bear Canyon on Mount Lemmon: the Ball Return gully comes first and the Lorax second. Eight routes mix sport and trad, all in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, mostly at 5.10. Reaching them takes real effort, with a steep drainage hike, some scrambling and a slab finish, past other Chessman sectors. The wider Chessman Area sits fairly low on the mountain and close to the highway, which keeps it usable for cooler-season cragging.
az_7_lorax_ball_return.approach: From the roadside drop-off, scramble up the rocky drainage for roughly 15 minutes (steep, with a little scrambling). At the fork near the base of the cliff, go right and continue another 15 minutes or so, passing the Bishop and Knight sectors. Then climb slabs, bearing left: the first gully is the Ball Return and the second is the Lorax.

az_attic_the.blurb: A shaded, quieter crag in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, part of the Isle of You area at roughly 5,300 feet. Eight routes, mostly sport with two trad lines, fall between 5.9 and 5.10, with most at 5.10. The routes are grouped in a lower and an upper cluster about 40 yards apart, under oak trees. The crag is fairly new and small flakes are still coming off, so a helmet is advised.

az_big_pine_towers_east_face.blurb: A steep east-facing wall on Mount Lemmon, part of Windy Point East, where a short stretch of the Catalina Highway packs in more climbs than anywhere else on the mountain. Eight routes, seven sport and one trad, all in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with most at 5.12. Expect tall endurance lines at the harder end alongside a few shorter 5.11s. The face goes into shade in the afternoon, which makes it a good pick in early fall and late spring. Strong climbers looking for sustained sport routes will like it most.

az_beach_the_3.blurb: A sport sector of Muscle Beach in Oak Creek Canyon, northern Arizona, at about 4,400 feet. It has eight bolted routes, all hard: two at 5.11, four at 5.12, one at 5.13 and one at 5.14. This is a place for strong sport climbers rather than anyone warming up. The sector is a short walk downstream past a neighbouring wall called The Surf, and at least some of its lines are short and technical.

az_chossy.blurb: A small boulder in the Hairpin Boulders area on the lower Catalina Highway of Mount Lemmon, outside Tucson. It has eight problems: mostly easy to moderate, from V0 to V4, plus one very hard project at the V10 level. Loose rocks around the base need cleaning, so check holds and landings carefully and bring pads. The canyon it sits in is shady in the afternoon and can feel chilly without sun, which suits the winter season.
